egtved.name: Egtved
egtved.summary: Village near Vejle in southern Denmark, known for a Bronze Age burial site found nearby.

funnelbeaker-culture.name: Funnelbeaker culture
funnelbeaker-culture.summary: A Neolithic archaeological culture in north-central Europe, about 4100 to 2800 BCE, that brought farming and husbandry to pottery-using hunter-gatherers north of the Elbe and Vistula rivers.

pitted-ware-culture.name: Pitted Ware culture
pitted-ware-culture.summary: A hunter-gatherer culture of coastal southern Scandinavia (c. 3500–2300 BC), known for maritime hunting and trade with farming communities before being absorbed into the Battle Axe culture.

nordic-bronze-age.name: Nordic Bronze Age
nordic-bronze-age.summary: A period of Scandinavian prehistory from about 2000/1750 to 500 BC, shaped by Central European metalworking traditions and maintaining trade links with Mycenaean Greece.

trundholm-sun-chariot.name: Trundholm sun chariot
trundholm-sun-chariot.summary: A Nordic Bronze Age bronze statue of a horse pulling a large disc on wheels, discovered in Denmark in 1902 and now held at the National Museum of Denmark.

pannonian-basin.name: Pannonian/Carpathian Basin
pannonian-basin.summary: A large lowland region in southeastern Central Europe, also called the Carpathian Basin, that formed the core of the historical Kingdom of Hungary and was a settlement zone for migrating steppe peoples.

mycenae.name: Mycenae
mycenae.summary: An archaeological site in Greece that was a major military stronghold and centre of Greek civilization in the second millennium BC, giving its name to the Mycenaean period.

mycenaean-greece.name: Mycenaean Greece
mycenaean-greece.summary: A late Bronze Age Greek civilization, lasting roughly 1750 to 1050 BC, marked by palatial states, art, and the Linear B writing system.

battle-axe-culture.name: Battle Axe culture
battle-axe-culture.summary: A Chalcolithic culture of southern Scandinavia and southwest Finland, about 2800 to 2300 BCE, thought to have spread Indo-European languages to the region and to have evolved into the Nordic Bronze Age.

uppland.name: Uppland
uppland.summary: A historical Swedish province north of Stockholm, famous for the highest concentration of runestones in the world and home to Sweden's oldest town and university.

oslofjord.name: Oslofjord
oslofjord.summary: A 120-kilometre inlet in southeastern Norway running from near Oslo south to the Skagerrak strait, called a fjord in Norwegian usage though not one in the strict geological sense.

bohusl-n.name: Bohuslän
bohusl-n.summary: A Swedish coastal province bordering Norway, held as a Norwegian territory from the 870s until ceded to Sweden by the 1658 Treaty of Roskilde.

corded-ware-culture.name: Corded Ware culture
corded-ware-culture.summary: A broad European archaeological culture from about 2900 to 2300 BC, likely descended from Yamnaya migrants and a probable vector for spreading Indo-European languages.

poetic-edda.name: Poetic Edda
poetic-edda.summary: A collection of anonymous Old Norse poems in alliterative verse, based on the medieval Icelandic Codex Regius manuscript, central to the study of Norse mythology.

snorri-sturluson.name: Snorri Sturluson
snorri-sturluson.summary: An Icelandic historian, poet and politician (1179–1241) credited with the Prose Edda and Heimskringla, key sources on Norse mythology and kings; he was assassinated in 1241.

prose-edda.name: Prose Edda
prose-edda.summary: An early 13th-century Old Norse textbook from Iceland, largely compiled by Snorri Sturluson, considered the fullest source for modern knowledge of Norse mythology.

m-ni.name: Máni
m-ni.summary: The Moon personified in Germanic mythology, described in the Poetic and Prose Eddas as brother of the sun goddess Sól.

john-lindow.name: John Lindow
john-lindow.summary: American philologist and professor emeritus of Old Norse and folklore at UC Berkeley, a well-known authority on Old Norse religion and literature.

n-tice-culture.name: Únětice culture
n-tice-culture.summary: An archaeological culture at the start of the Central European Bronze Age, dated to about 2300 to 1600 BC, known from sites across the Czech Republic, Slovakia, Poland and Germany.

bell-beaker-culture.name: Bell Beaker culture
bell-beaker-culture.summary: A Bronze Age archaeological culture named for its inverted-bell drinking vessel, spreading across Western Europe from around 2800 BCE.

jutland.name: Jutland
jutland.summary: Peninsula in Northern Europe forming continental Denmark and part of northern Germany, flat with open heaths in the west and fertile lakes and forests in the east.

bog-iron.name: Bog iron
bog-iron.summary: An impure iron deposit that forms in bogs and swamps from iron carried in groundwater, historically smelted as a natural iron source.

haplogroup-r1a.name: Haplogroup R1a1a1
haplogroup-r1a.summary: A Y-chromosome lineage spanning Scandinavia to Central Asia and South Asia, whose main subclade diversified roughly 3,400 to 5,800 years ago and is central to debates on Indo-European origins.

western-steppe-herders.name: Western Steppe Herders
western-steppe-herders.summary: A genetic ancestry group first identified in Chalcolithic steppe populations around 5000 BC, descended from a merger of Eastern and Caucasus hunter-gatherers, later spreading widely across Eurasia.

assur.name: Assur
assur.summary: An ancient city on the Tigris River, capital of the Middle and Neo-Assyrian Empires, occupied for roughly 3,000 years until sacked in the mid-3rd century CE.

sintashta-culture.name: Sintashta culture
sintashta-culture.summary: A Middle Bronze Age archaeological culture of the Southern Urals (c. 2200–1900 BCE), thought to be the origin of the Indo-Iranian languages and the earliest known chariots, with fortified, militaristic settlements.

rigveda.name: Rigveda
rigveda.summary: An ancient collection of Vedic Sanskrit hymns, the oldest known Vedic text and one of the four sacred Hindu Vedas, most likely composed between about 1500 and 1000 BCE in northwestern India.

odsherred-municipality.name: Odsherred
odsherred-municipality.summary: A district and municipality in Region Sjælland, Denmark, covering part of northwestern Zealand.

zealand.name: Zealand
zealand.summary: The largest and most populous island of Denmark, home to the capital Copenhagen, making up about 40% of the country's population.

egtved-girl.name: Egtved Girl
egtved-girl.summary: Nordic Bronze Age girl (c. 1390–1370 BC), aged about 16 to 18, whose remarkably preserved remains were found near Egtved, Denmark, in 1921.

national-museum-of-denmark.name: National Museum of Denmark
national-museum-of-denmark.summary: Denmark's largest museum of cultural history, in Copenhagen, covering Danish and foreign cultures worldwide and overseeing national archaeology, ethnography and treasure collections.

nebra-sky-disc.name: Nebra sky disc
nebra-sky-disc.summary: A Bronze Age bronze disc inlaid with gold symbols of the sun, moon, and stars, found near Nebra, Germany in 1999 and dated to about 1800 to 1600 BC; the oldest known depiction of astronomical phenomena.

tanumshede.name: Tanumshede
tanumshede.summary: A locality in Västra Götaland County, Sweden, and seat of Tanum Municipality, with about 1,700 inhabitants in 2010.

single-grave-culture.name: Single Grave culture
single-grave-culture.summary: A Chalcolithic culture (c. 2800–2200 BC) on the North European Plain, marked by single burials with battle axes, amber beads and pottery, and linked to the Corded Ware culture.
